limitations: Case A is exactly represented by the cubic Hermite element, so its tip-load errors are a round-off floor (~1e-13) rather than a converged discretisation; the measured order comes from the uniform-load interior field.  Euler-Bernoulli theory itself ignores transverse shear, which at L/h = 10 is a ~2 % model-level difference that the 1 % comparison to the same theory does not measure.

Case B uses soft simple support (w = 0, rotations free) and a/t = 100, so the Mindlin transverse-shear compliance is a ~1e-4 relative model difference against the Kirchhoff oracle.  The plate centre-deflection error is not monotone in the mesh, so the plate rate is graded on the L2 deflection-field norm.

Case C enforces plane strain (u_z = 0) rather than modelling the closed or open ends; the Lame sigma_r/sigma_theta fields are independent of the end condition, but sigma_z = 2 nu A corresponds to plane strain only.  Stresses are reported after standard nodal recovery: the raw Gauss-point values are first order, and both sets are in result.json.

All three cases are linear-elastic, small-displacement, single-physics checks.  They certify element kernels and load/boundary handling, not mesh quality on curved geometry, plasticity, contact or dynamics.
